name: curzon_ahlborn_max_power
title: Endoreversible Carnot engine at maximum power (Curzon-Ahlborn)
summary: Heat-transfer-limited (endoreversible) Carnot engine between two reservoirs: the cycle temperatures that maximise the power output follow from the Lagrange undetermined-multiplier equations of the original ($ifnot MinMax branch, solved as a square steady system). At the optimum the efficiency is 1 - sqrt(T_L/T_H) whatever the conductances.

verification.summary: No stored solution exists in the plain-text source. The solved model was checked analytically: eta agrees with 1 - sqrt(T_L/T_H) to 3.29e-11 absolute (6.36e-11 relative) and W_dot equals Q_dot_H - Q_dot_L to 0.00e+00 W (machine precision). T_1, T_2, W_dot and eta also match the closed-form Curzon-Ahlborn optimum with unequal conductances to 8 significant digits.
verification.reference: Closed-form Curzon-Ahlborn efficiency eta = 1 - sqrt(T_L/T_H) and the closed-form optimum of the conductance-limited engine; energy balance of the cycle
verification.notes: Residuals: |eta - (1-sqrt(T_L/T_H))| = 3.29e-11 (relative 6.36e-11); |W_dot - (Q_dot_H-Q_dot_L)| = 0.00e+00 W. Analytical optimum T_1 = (A*T_H + B*sqrt(T_H*T_L))/(A+B), T_2 = T_1*sqrt(T_L/T_H): 712.376276 / 203.678426 degC, W 400639.4 W, eta 0.51616873 - all match the .sol.
